notes: Canonical paper for the model family named in the brief's category 2. Resolved via `uvx opencite search "LaBraM large brain model generic representations tremendous EEG"` (hit [1], DOI 10.48550/arxiv.2405.18765, OpenAlex W4399198086, 414 citations) and confirmed by `uvx opencite lookup "arXiv:2405.18765"`, which reports the venue as "The Twelfth International Conference on Learning Representations, 2024". The retrieved PDF's running header reads "Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024", so venue is recorded as ICLR 2024 with the arXiv record as the retrieval source. LICENCE -- the abs-license block on https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.18765 links http://arxiv.org/licenses/nonexclusive-distrib/1.0/, whose canonical text is "I grant arXiv.org a perpetual, non-exclusive license to distribute this article." That grants arXiv distribution rights, not third parties, so it is not a Creative Commons licence and preprint-cc-arxiv does not apply. I attempted to find a better-licensed copy on OpenReview, where ICLR proceedings are usually CC BY 4.0: api2.openreview.net returned HTTP 403 ChallengeRequiredError (bot challenge) for both the note-id and forum queries, so I could not positively identify the licence of any OpenReview copy. Under deny-by-default that means unknown / redistribution_ok false; the arXiv PDF was downloaded, hashed, then DELETED from the entry folder rather than committed. source.md is retained as internal research notes under fair use. Re-attempt: fetch the OpenReview record for the ICLR 2024 forum when the endpoint is reachable; if it is CC BY 4.0, that copy can be archived and this entry promoted to pdf_status archived. TITLE -- the arXiv title ends "... with Tremendous EEG Data in BCI"; the ICLR proceedings title omits "in BCI". The bib entry uses the arXiv form, which is what opencite returned and what the retrieved PDF's own title block shows. EXTRACTION -- markitdown; body prose and the Table 1/Table 2 results tables survive legibly, but Figures 3-5 (the pre-training curves and the data-scaling sweep) render as character soup, so the data-scaling claim on the card is quoted from the surrounding prose rather than read off the figure. Hence md_quality: rough.
